brief.t: Week ending Oct 22: cotton commitments 5,872 '000 running bales for 2026/27 (2,107 shipped, 3,765 outstanding) = **49% of USDA's 12.30 m 480-lb bales** export forecast, vs a 5-yr norm of 56% by week 12. (USDA's statistical bales are converted to the export-sales running-bale basis at 0.970 running bales per 480-lb bale, the median ratio of final export-sales shipments to USDA's final exports over the last 5 seasons: 12.30m ≈ 11,925 '000 running bales.) Commitments are +17% vs a year ago. At the usual seasonal pace that points to about **10.81 m 480-lb bales** (-12% vs USDA) — USDA looks too high; risk of a cut.

Shipments 18% of target (norm 16%). To reach USDA's number, shipments need to average 245 '000 running bales/week for the remaining 40 weeks vs 171 over the last 4 weeks; new sales need 176/week (allowing for about 1,000 carried into next season) vs 186 recently (5-yr avg for these weeks 171).
Net sales 217 vs 202 the week before (+7%), +55% vs the same week last year and +14% vs the 5-yr average. Shipments 164 vs 204 (-20%), -11% vs last year, +29% vs the 5-yr average.
Net sales 1,815 (-11% y/y, -11% vs 5-yr avg); shipments 2,107 (+20% y/y); outstanding sales 3,765 (+15% y/y); next-season sales on the books 612.

ICE cotton averaged 80.73¢ in the reporting week (Fri–Thu; low 79.60, high 82.10), +0.3% vs the week before (80.47¢) and +25.9% vs the same week last year (64.13¢). The week's low was -1.1% vs last week's average. Net sales were +50% vs their recent trend and +14% vs the 5-yr average for this week. Prices were little changed, so the week's sales mostly reflect underlying demand. Price-sensitive buyers active this week: China 52.1, Turkey 40.8, Vietnam 35.0, Indonesia 26.4.
Net sales 217 '000 running bales (4-wk avg 186); shipments 164. Main buyers: China 52.1, Turkey 40.8, Vietnam 35.0, Indonesia 26.4. Net reductions: El Salvador -0.0, South Korea -0.0, Guatemala -0.0.

Buying more US than usual: Vietnam (pace implies 58% US share of its 8.30 import forecast vs 34% usual); Indonesia (pace implies 23% US share of its 2.10 import forecast vs 19% usual). Buying less US than usual: China (8% vs 34% usual); Turkey (16% vs 31% usual); Bangladesh (5% vs 9% usual). Across these destinations, the sales pace adds up to -1.57 m 480-lb bales vs their usual US-origin volumes — argues against raising USDA's number.

Main competitors (Brazil, Australia, Afr. Fr. Zone): exportable surplus -2.26 vs 2025/26 (Australia -2.43), and USDA has their combined exports -0.40 — less competition for US cotton. India is not competing for export business this season: supply is 1.33× its own use (it exports in volume only when this is about 1.5× or more), so it is counted as an importer. Importers with tighter own supply vs use than last year: China (-1.30; imports 7.00 vs 7.25), Pakistan (-0.85; imports 5.10 vs 4.40), Turkey (-0.78; imports 5.00 vs 4.73). Better supplied: India (+1.56). World use 123.08 (+1.9% y/y), world trade 44.72 (-0.6%). USDA has the US at 28% of world exports vs 27% last season.
Shipments usually concentrate in the next three months for Mexico (25% of its season), China (22% of its season), Peru (21% of its season).

Export outlook vs USDA: **below USDA's 12.30 m 480-lb bales**. Pointing lower: sales pace, destination buying. Pointing higher: competitor exports. Less competition usually shows up later in the season, once rival origins run short — watch whether US sales accelerate into the new year before reading the slow start as lost demand.
